binders: There exists a real constant c, chosen before and uniformly over all subsequent data.
For every type ι with a finite-type structure and every type Ω with a measurable-space structure.
For every probability measure μ on Ω.
For every finite family X : ι → Ω → ℝ of real-valued functions and every coefficient family a : ι → ℝ.
Given a witness that the universal finite set of indices is nonempty.
Within each regime conclusion, for every real threshold t.
hypotheses: Every Xᵢ is μ-integrable and centered: ∫ Xᵢ dμ = 0.
For every i, the exponential-moment gauge of Xᵢ is strictly below ∞ in ENNReal.
The family (Xᵢ)ᵢ is mutually independent with respect to μ.
The first conclusion is conditional on A > 0; the second is conditional on A = 0.
conclusions: Let K = maxᵢ (gaugeμ(Xᵢ)).toReal, A = K² Σᵢ aᵢ², and B = K maxᵢ |aᵢ|. If A > 0, then for every t ≥ 0, μ({ω | |Σᵢ aᵢ Xᵢ(ω)| ≥ t}).toReal ≤ 2 exp(-c min(t²/A, t/B)).
With the same K, A, and B, if A = 0, then for every t ≥ 0, μ({ω | |Σᵢ aᵢ Xᵢ(ω)| ≥ t}).toReal ≤ 2 when t = 0 and ≤ 0 when t ≠ 0.
mathematical_definitions: For a real function X on Ω, gaugeμ(X) is the ENNReal infimum of the scales s such that X is measurable, s ≠ 0, s ≠ ∞, exp(|X|/s.toReal) is μ-integrable, and ∫ exp(|X|/s.toReal) dμ ≤ 2.
K is the maximum over the nonempty finite index set of the real conversions of the individual gauges.
A = K² Σᵢ aᵢ² is the quadratic scale and B = K maxᵢ |aᵢ| is the linear scale.
The probability in each conclusion is represented as the real conversion of μ applied to the indicated tail event.
translation.proposition_plain_english: There is a universal positive constant c such that every nonempty finite independent family of measurable, integrable, mean-zero real random variables with finite exponential-moment gauges satisfies a Bernstein-type tail estimate for every real coefficient vector. Using the largest gauge K, the usual quadratic scale A = K² times the sum of squared coefficients, and the linear scale B = K times the largest absolute coefficient, the tail is bounded by twice an exponential of minus c times the smaller of t²/A and t/B whenever A is positive. The statement separately covers the degenerate case A = 0, where it bounds the tail by 2 at threshold zero and by 0 at every positive threshold.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The index type must be finite and nonempty; no empty-family case is stated.
Only real-valued random variables and real coefficients are covered.
The ambient measure must be a probability measure, and every variable must separately be measurable, integrable, and exactly centered.
Every individual gauge must be strictly below ENNReal infinity before it is converted to a real number and maximized.
The gauge is an infimum over nonzero finite admissible scales; its definition does not itself assert that the infimum is positive or attained.

The positive-A formula is guarded by A > 0, avoiding its t²/A denominator at A = 0. Although B has no separate positivity guard, the finite nonempty real setting and A > 0 mathematically force K and some coefficient magnitude to be positive, hence B > 0.
The degenerate A = 0 branch is substantive: for every t > 0 its right-hand side is zero, so it forces the weighted sum to have zero probability of exceeding every positive threshold.
Thresholds are restricted to t ≥ 0. At t = 0 the degenerate bound is 2, which is weaker than the probability-measure bound 1 but avoids a false zero bound.

The target states two implications, one under A > 0 and one under A = 0. Their practical exhaustiveness uses the nonnegativity of K² and the coefficient-square sum rather than an explicit A ≥ 0 hypothesis.
The use of μ.real is harmless under the probability-measure assumption because event measures are finite, but in general ENNReal.toReal would collapse infinity to zero.
ambiguities: The local gauge is recognizable as a ψ₁/Orlicz-type exponential-moment scale, but no conventional name or normalization is supplied in the dossier; the exact infimum definition above is therefore controlling.

The target does not explain whether the explicit A = 0 conclusion is intended as a theorem-derived endpoint extension or as part of the named mathematical result; it is nevertheless unambiguously part of the formal proposition.

The relationship between a zero value of the infimum-defined gauge and almost-sure vanishing of X is not encoded in the definition itself, yet the A = 0 branch asserts the corresponding zero positive-threshold tails for the weighted sum.
